name: network_log_summary
description: Normalise three log grammars into one table and account for every line: web (Apache/nginx common and combined), Squid's native access.log, and upper-case KEY=VALUE firewall records. No other format is parsed; a line that fits none is unparsed and says so. Every source line is in normalized.tsv or unparsed.tsv with its line number and the byte offset and length of the line in the stream read (the decompressed stream for gzip), so a row finds its line in the evidence. Time is three columns (a web line with no offset, an RFC 5424 time and a line with no timestamp each say which they are): timestamp_raw as written, timestamp_utc only where the line gives enough to derive it (a web offset, Squid epoch seconds, an ISO 8601 firewall prefix with a zone), and timezone_source; a syslog stamp has no year or zone and is never read as UTC. The file is read as bytes: invalid UTF-8 is substituted and counted (decoding_substituted), CRLF is counted, a line over max_line_bytes is located and not read, gzip expansion is capped (max_expanded_bytes) and a cap or a corrupt stream is a structured error that keeps the rows read before it and names the offset (complete and ok false), and aggregates hold at most max_distinct_values per category (a key is cut at 512 characters) with the overflow counted: a ranking is exact only while distinct_cap_reached is null. A leading byte order mark is stripped and counted. Forwarded headers, NAT addresses and action labels are what the logging device wrote, not facts about the sender. SENSITIVE: the request target and the combined-format referer (a column of its own) are redacted (user-info, token-shaped path text and every query value withheld; parameter names stay), the table has no raw line and the answer none. Redaction is by shape; run it as a job with secret_output: true. write_values: true (jobs only, refused elsewhere) writes the unparsed lines and the original targets to $OUT/network-log-values.jsonl, mode 0600, created before anything is read; a second run in the same job is refused by name.

path.description: A plain-text or gzip-compressed log in one of the three grammars

out_dir.description: An empty directory under work/ (in a job, under $OUT; work/<your agent id>/name is mapped to $OUT/name) for normalized.tsv and unparsed.tsv. It is private (0700, files 0600)

format.description: auto (default: web, then squid, then firewall per line), web, squid or firewall

top.description: Aggregate rows returned per category (default 20); every parsed line is in normalized.tsv

write_values.description: Write the text of every unparsed line and the original target and referer of every redacted one to $OUT/network-log-values.jsonl (default false; lines are written as JSON escapes, byte for byte). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; a file already there is refused, and a run that stops before it wrote a value gives the file back

max_line_bytes.description: A line longer than this is located in unparsed.tsv and not read (default 1048576, at least 4096)

max_expanded_bytes.description: How far a gzip stream may expand (default 4294967296, at least 1048576); past it the read stops, the answer says where and is not ok

max_distinct_values.description: Distinct values counted per aggregate category (default 200000); occurrences of values past it are counted in distinct_cap_reached
